title: What are the best AI portfolio trackers?
summary: The best AI portfolio trackers for the brokerage you already have, with prices and who each fits, from the team that makes Astor.
body_markdown:
## Which AI portfolio trackers are worth using?


### Mezzi: best for advice across every account you have


Mezzi pairs an AI chat with net worth tracking and portfolio analysis, and it’s offered by StockTalk, Inc., an SEC-registered investment adviser. It connects brokerage accounts, workplace retirement plans, IRAs, HSAs, 529s and crypto through Plaid, Finicity and SnapTrade, with unlimited connections on every plan. The chat answers from your account data, and the free plan allows 10 AI insights a month.


On the paid Advisory and Concierge plans, a beta feature called Delegations can send a daily summary of the news moving your portfolio by email or push notification. Mezzi doesn’t place trades, and it’s on iPhone and the web for US residents only.


### PortfolioPilot: best for a detailed second opinion


PortfolioPilot is offered by Global Predictions, an SEC-registered investment adviser, and it reviews your whole portfolio and makes recommendations. It connects to more than 12,000 US and Canadian institutions and tracks brokerage accounts, 401(k)s, IRAs, crypto, real estate and private equity, with cost basis. Its AI assistant answers questions about your portfolio in plain language, and a weekly email recaps how it changed along with your top recommendations.


The free plan tracks net worth but doesn’t include the assistant or advice. Gold costs $29 a month or $240 a year with limited assistant use, Platinum $99 a month or $588 a year and Pro $149 a month or $1,188 a year, each with a 10-day trial. It’s web only and can’t place trades, and because prices update once a day after the close, it suits a periodic review more than following today’s moves.


### Delta: best for daily explanations across stocks and crypto


Delta, part of the eToro group, tracks stocks, ETFs, crypto and forex. On its PRO and PRO+ plans, a feature called “What’s going on?” writes a two-paragraph summary of what moved your portfolio today and lists your top three movers. It connects to brokers, exchanges and wallets read-only, takes CSV imports and sends push notifications for price changes and end-of-day updates.


Delta says the prices in the table above can vary by location, and AI use is capped on PRO and unlimited on PRO+. You can’t trade from Delta, and most broker connections sync once a day.


### Magnifi: best for finding new investment ideas


Magnifi comes from Magnifi LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser owned by The TIFIN Group. It connects brokerage accounts, IRAs, 401(k)s and 529s through aggregators like Plaid. Its chat gives insights on your portfolio, and its app follows the news, earnings dates and analyst upgrades that affect your holdings. Premium adds weekly summaries with a portfolio health-check score.


You can also place commission-free trades from the platform, and Magnifi says it won’t execute one without your confirmation. It leans more toward finding your next investment than explaining the ones you have.


### Kubera: best for net worth beyond a brokerage account


Kubera tracks almost anything you own, from brokerage and retirement accounts to crypto wallets, real estate and private investments, through aggregators including Plaid, MX, Yodlee and SnapTrade. It doesn’t have its own chatbot, so you connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and ask them about your balance sheet.


Its recap shows how your net worth changed since yesterday, but it doesn’t explain the cause or send news alerts. Essentials costs $250 a year after a 14-day trial, on the web and as an installable mobile web app. Kubera says it isn’t a registered financial adviser.


### Astor: our top pick for knowing why your portfolio moved


Astor connects to the brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts you already have at most major US institutions, like Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase, and follows every position you own along with the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them.[At a glance](https://www.astor.app/blog/at-a-glance) gives you a daily chart and the Astor Take, two lines on what moved your money today and why. On Pro and Max, when something crosses a line you care about, Astor texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do, and it stays quiet when nothing matters.


You can[text Astor](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) over iMessage or WhatsApp to ask a follow-up about what you own, and set[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) , like a check before a company you own reports. Astor is an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its recommendations are personalized investment advice, and you make every decision.


Astor is free to start with no card, and the free plan includes a recap after each close and one custom alert at a time. Pro and Max are in the table above and on our[pricing page](https://www.astor.app/pricing) . There’s no Android app or web app and it’s US only. It also doesn’t track real estate or help with tax filing. The AI can be wrong, which is why every alert links to its reasoning and sources and you make the call.
